title: physical RTX 5090 rank-1 qualification of malaiwah/Qwen3.8-27B-EXL3-K5K6-context
claim_scope: hard-limit proof on one physical NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 32,607 MiB total, 32,149 MiB free with the GPU idle, which vLLM sizes as 31.4 GiB usable. This supersedes the engine-budget simulation in receipts/native-mtp-8mp-amendment.json, which was measured on a rental RTX PRO 6000 with vLLM hard-budgeted to 30.24 GiB of a 95.6 GiB card. Throughput measured here is never comparable with rental numbers and no number in this receipt is differenced against them.

qualified_profile.delta_from_published_card: the card prints --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 and sets no allocator config. Change those two things and nothing else: 0.97 -> 0.955 and add -e PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True. Window, MTP depth, image ceiling, KV dtype, sequence count and cudagraph mode are unchanged from the card.

gpu_memory_utilization_justification.why: with the GPU idle the card reports 32,149 MiB free of 32,607 MiB total, and vLLM sizes its budget off the usable figure: it logged 'Free memory on device (30.9/31.4 GiB) on startup'. 0.97 x 31.4 GiB = 30.45 GiB started fine and served text, but left only 26.5 MiB free at peak, so the vision tower could not get the 62 MiB it needed for a 7 MP image. 0.955 x 31.4 GiB = 29.98 GiB keeps 265,122 KV tokens, still 1.01x concurrency at 262,144, and leaves roughly half a GiB of card for transient vision activations. Both values are at or under the 0.97 ceiling the acceptance gate allows.
gpu_memory_utilization_justification.why_not_higher: raising utilisation is self-defeating for large-image work: at 0.97 with expandable_segments the engine simply spent the recovered bytes on KV (272,570 -> 280,017 tokens) and still OOMed with 26.5 MiB free.
gpu_memory_utilization_justification.what_was_not_sacrificed: max_pixels stayed at the published 8,388,608, MTP stayed at depth 3 and the window stayed at 262,144; only KV slack was given up

seven_megapixel_ceiling_verdict.question: is the vision-tower OOM a hard 32 GB ceiling for a seven-megapixel request, or only a slack problem?
seven_megapixel_ceiling_verdict.answer: a slack problem, but max_pixels is the WRONG knob: lowering the image ceiling at fixed utilisation makes it strictly worse
seven_megapixel_ceiling_verdict.mechanism_measured: vLLM sizes the KV cache to consume whatever is left of the budget after profiling, so every byte freed anywhere else is immediately spent on KV and the slack never materialises. Lowering max_pixels lowers the profiled peak activation, which enlarges KV, which leaves less room for the real vision activation than before.

evidence.outcome: OOM, sooner and with less headroom

seven_megapixel_ceiling_verdict.hard_ceiling_evidence: the identical 236,824-token plus 7,077,888-pixel request succeeds on this same physical card at utilisation 0.955 with the full 8,388,608 pixel ceiling, so 32 GB is sufficient for the request; only the budget split was wrong
seven_megapixel_ceiling_verdict.which_knob_first: turn gpu_memory_utilization down, not max_pixels. 0.955 is the measured value that passes: it keeps the full 8,388,608 ceiling, native 262,144 and MTP depth 3, and costs only KV slack (280,017 -> 265,122 tokens, still 1.01x concurrency at 262,144). Lowering max_pixels at 0.97 does not help and silently downscales large images as well.

prefix_caching_control_arm.why: the runtime image lacks upstream vLLM #51113, so a prefill chunk ending mid-block can publish a truncated GDN state that a later request over a shared prefix could consume. This arm reruns the needle and the decode bench with prefix caching explicitly disabled, everything else equal.
prefix_caching_control_arm.material_finding: the published profile already runs with prefix caching OFF: the engine config for the unmodified card command reports enable_prefix_caching=False with no flag from us, and every scheduler log line reports 'Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%'. This build disables prefix caching for the hybrid mamba model, so the #51113 poisoning path is never exercised by this profile and the flag is a no-op here.

correctness_caveats: the runtime image lacks upstream vLLM #51113 (mamba align-mode chunk splitting past last_cache_position). Each long-context gate therefore ran in a freshly started server process, and an explicit --no-enable-prefix-caching control arm is published. The material finding is that this profile already runs with prefix caching off, so the poisoning path is not exercised.
gate 6 intentionally reuses gate 2's process at the same request length, because in-process recovery of the allocation is the property it tests.
gate 4's 24/30 sits exactly on the acceptance threshold; it is a pass with no margin, and the per-case answers are published so a reader can audit it.

gate 5's three runs are warmed and single-stream on an otherwise idle card, but they follow two 261,794-token requests in the same process, which is the state a long-context user would actually decode in.
